ai.description: This 20–30 cm snake has a glossy, iridescent purplish-brown body with a pale yellow venter. It features a blunt, shield-like tail and a pointed snout adapted for burrowing. Family: Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhinophis travancoricus* is best distinguished by its blunt, shield-like tail ending in a single, large, thickened terminal scale that is distinctly keeled or notched.
ai.habitat: Rhinophis travancoricus inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found in leaf litter at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Rhinophis travancoricus* is a nocturnal, burrowing snake that spends most of its life underground, emerging to the surface primarily after heavy monsoon rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhinophis travancoricus* is ovoviviparous, producing small litters of 3–8 live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Travancore earth snake is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, primarily occurring in the Indian states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu at mid-to-high elevations.
